_note: WHAT TO PUBLISH. Read by tools/build_packs.py (PLAN.md 3.2/3.3, phase 0.3).
THIS FILE HOLDS PUBLISHING DECISIONS ONLY. Title and description are NOT here -- they
are read out of each campaign's own campaign.json, because duplicating them would let
the store page and the game disagree about what a campaign is called. What lives here
is what campaign.json cannot know: the pack id, its version, and whether the game
requires it.
`version` IS BUMPED BY HAND AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Publishing is the one step in this
project with no undo -- a client that has downloaded v2 will not look again until it
sees v3 -- so the number is a decision rather than a side effect of running a script.
build_packs.py compares what it built against the published packs.json and REFUSES to
write a manifest whose bytes changed under an unchanged version, which is the mistake
this guards: content edited, script re-run, and every existing install left stale with
no way to notice.
`required` is the owner's split (2026-09-03): true means the boot sequence fetches it
with nobody asked, false means it is offered in DOWNLOAD MORE and fetched only when a
player picks it. How To Play is the tutorial, so the front door would be lying without
it. Everything after the first campaign is expected to be optional.

_note_v3: V3, 2026-09-07: scenario 5 is the duel across one ford (PLAN.md 15.x / card #67).
New map -- seed 207152, River, 112x112, two players on room for three -- and the
mission changed shape with it: mode `scenario` carrying two ANDed win rows that
spell out the ordinary conquest condition, so 'destroy the enemy' can be READ on
screen at 0/1 instead of being an unstated rule. The owner's spec, and the reason
the mode moved is that `ScenarioDef` refuses `last_man_standing` carrying
objectives -- outside SCENARIO mode `ObjectiveSystem` never runs, so the rows would
have been dead text under a tracker stuck at 0/1 all match.
V2 REACHED PHONES AND WAS PLAYED, which is why this is v3 and not a v2 rebuild: the
live manifest read version 2 when this was built (checked, 2026-09-07), and the
owner played scenarios 1-4 off it. Overwriting v2 in place would leave every
install that has it permanently on the old scenario 5 with nothing on screen to say
so. The guard refused the rebuild before the version was touched, as designed.
_note_v2: V2, 2026-09-06: scenario 4 is the dragon claim (PLAN.md 13.2 / 15.8). New map with
the nest, the mother and a 75-unit army; mode `scenario` with two win rows; starts
in age 4. v1 was a mission whose briefing promised a dragon its map had not got.
⚠️ THE OWNER ASKED FOR 'campaign_howtoplay_v1.zip' REPACKED AND THAT FILENAME IS NOT
WHAT SHIPPED, on purpose. build_packs.py REFUSED the rebuild -- content changed under
an unchanged version -- and it is right: a client holding v1 checks the manifest,
sees v1, and never looks again. Overwriting the v1 zip in place would leave every
existing install permanently on the old scenario 4 with nothing on screen to say so,
which is exactly the mistake the guard was written for. So the file to copy is
_note_v4: V4, 2026-09-12: THE CONTENT DID NOT CHANGE. THE CONTAINER DID.
The art pack made `build_packs.py` STORE already-compressed formats instead of
deflating them -- PNG is deflated already, and deflating 320 MB of atlas pages
for a measured 1% costs minutes on every build. That policy is per-SUFFIX and not
per-kind, on purpose, so it reached this campaign's icons too and moved its bytes.
The guard refused the rebuild and was right to: it compares digests, and it cannot
tell a re-encoded container from edited content. Bumping is the safe direction --
every install converges on a file we have actually checked -- and the alternative
was to freeze the old encoding for campaigns forever so that two kinds of pack
would be built two different ways. The owner pre-authorised version bumps for
⚠️ SO THIS IS THE FIRST BUMP IN THE PROJECT THAT BUYS A PLAYER NOTHING, and it is
worth knowing that a build-script change can cost one. If it ever matters, the
lever is the compression policy and not the guard.

_note: A TEST PACK, and the only reason it exists is that the OPTIONAL download path had
nothing to exercise it: How To Play is required, so DOWNLOAD MORE was empty the
moment it was installed and the browse-and-pick half could not be tried on a phone.
The owner asked for one on 2026-09-03 -- 'does not need to be playable only
downloadable'. It is in fact playable, because deriving it from a real campaign was
less work than breaking one.
`derive` IS WHY THERE IS NO SECOND COPY IN GIT. It rewrites campaign.json's name and
description as the zip is built, so this costs one entry here instead of 2.2 MB of
duplicated content that would drift from the original -- and, more importantly, a
real scenarios/HowToPlayDummy/ folder would be picked up by the EDITOR's dev
override and show as a second campaign in every developer's campaign list forever.
`folder` MUST DIFFER FROM THE ORIGINAL'S. It is the install directory, the identity
Campaigns shadows by, and the key into user://campaign_progress.json -- so reusing
'HowToPlay' would not install a second campaign, it would overwrite the first and
inherit its progress.
DELETE THIS ENTRY once there is a real optional campaign to list.
V2 FOR THE SAME REASON AND ON THE SAME DAY. It derives from the same folder, so its
bytes moved when scenario 4 did and the guard refused it too. Bumped rather than
left behind: two campaigns both called How To Play, holding two different scenario
4s, is precisely the confusion this entry's `folder` rule above is worried about.
V3, 2026-09-07, AND THE THIRD TIME THIS HAS HAPPENED FOR THE SAME STRUCTURAL REASON.
It derives from `scenarios/HowToPlay`, so every edit to that folder moves this pack's
bytes and the guard refuses it until the version follows. Worth naming as a standing
cost of `derive` rather than rediscovering it each time: this entry can never be left
on an older version than the campaign it copies.
_note_v4: V4, 2026-09-12, AND THE FOURTH TIME THIS ENTRY HAS FOLLOWED ITS ORIGINAL. This
time not even the original's content moved -- see `howtoplay`'s own _note_v4: the
packer now stores PNGs rather than deflating them, so every pack's bytes moved at
once. The standing cost of `derive` noted above applies unchanged.

_note: THE ART, 2026-09-12, AND IT IS TWO PACKS BECAUSE OF WHERE THE BYTES ARE.
The art agent measured the staged tree on 2026-09-04: 314 MB, of which the
player-colour variants are 224 MB -- SEVENTY-FOUR PERCENT. Their conclusion, and
the owner's decision on 2026-09-12, is that base-against-colour is the only split
that means anything. `terrain / units / UI` is not a seam: terrain is under 1 MB
and UI art is not in the bake output at all.
⚠️ THE SPLIT IS ONLY SAFE BECAUSE THE SEAM ALREADY FALLS BACK, and that was
verified before it was chosen rather than assumed. `_atlas_path_for_skin` takes a
tinted path only `if FileAccess.file_exists(tinted)` and otherwise returns the
untinted one -- so a player without the colours pack is GREY and plays perfectly.
Had it resolved to the magenta placeholder instead, the split would have been off
the table and this would be one 314 MB required download.
`select` IS WHAT DIVIDES THEM and the two halves are disjoint by construction --
`base` is every `atlas` and every `ages` value, `colours` is every tinted sibling
of those. Neither is a directory listing: build_packs.py resolves both out of
visuals.json, so a retired bake leaves the pack the moment nothing points at it.
NO `folder`. Art is MOUNTED, not installed, and `PackDef` refuses a mounted pack
carrying one -- so an entry with a folder here publishes a row every client will
reject on arrival.
VERSION BUMPS ARE THE SAME HAND-EDITED DECISION AS EVERYWHERE ELSE, and the art
agent's answer to 'what identifies a bake' was: nothing in the atlas does, hash
the content. `attribution.actor` never moves between rebakes of one asset and
`generator.isobake_commit` is absent from 67 of the staged atlases. The guard
already in this script IS the mechanism -- a rebake moves the digest, the build
refuses, and the number follows.

packs.title: Game art
packs.description: Every unit, building, terrain and prop in the game. Without it Age of Dragons draws coloured placeholder shapes -- it runs, but nothing looks like what it is.

_note: THE PLAYER COLOURS. Optional, and three quarters of the art by weight.
21 units x 8 colours. A player who skips this sees every unit in its untinted
bake -- readable, playable, and the thing it costs is telling whose army is whose
at a glance, which in an eight-player match is not nothing.
⚠️ WHETHER THIS SPLITS FURTHER -- eight packs of ~28 MB, a device fetching only
the colours it plays -- IS A REAL QUESTION AND IS NOT ANSWERED. The art agent
raised it and it now turns on gameplay rather than on bytes: a player does not
choose their opponents' colours, and an AI match hands them out. So the set a
device needs is not knowable at download time, which is why it is one pack today.

packs.title: Player colours
packs.description: Tinted art for all eight player colours. Without it every unit shows in its base colours and you tell armies apart by position rather than by sight.
